orchestrator_note: Protocol default routes LOW to debt regardless of severity. R2/R3/R4 are routed to repair instead, as an explicit orchestrator deviation: R1 forces a repair round anyway, and all three are <=3-line corrections in the same files R1 opens, of the same defect class (prose in a document of record contradicting the code or artifact beside it). Three debt blocks plus a future PR costs more than the fix. Deviation is recorded here so the next round's reviewer sees it.

findings.blocks_because: committed artifact of record (specs/decisions/) states a mechanism that is false about its own enforcing case - a reader takes an ADR as verified-correct
findings.claim: ADR-024's Consequences section states the wrong mechanism for its own shipped case: it attributes `replans: 0` to a mid-run adoption refusal, when the shipped case is a PRE-execution refusal whose replan simply repeated the plan - and no case in this PR exercises the mid-run adoption path for the new rule at all.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-024-document-root-is-not-an-answer.md:131-137 - "refused BEFORE execution it is one replan ...; refused at a mid-run adoption point it ends the run ... - which is why the shipped case asserts `replans: 0`." The shipped case (evals/adversarial/plan-lint-refuses-a-document-root-extract.json) carries a single `stub_plan`, so the refusal fires at agent.py:721 (the pre-execution branch, `if gap := plan_gap(task, steps)`), the gap note IS sent to the planner (that is what `planner_note_contains: "WebArea"` grades), and `replans` stays 0 only because `stub_planner` repeats its last plan and agent.py:740 (`new_steps == steps`) ends the run. Observed reason string: "plan rejected before execution: the plan reads 'extract' off 'WebArea' ...; the replan did not close the gap". Under the ADR's own stated rule for the branch the case actually takes, `replans` should be 1; it is 0 for a reason the ADR does not state. `adopt()` (agent.py:688-717), the mid-run path the sentence describes, is never reached by any case carrying a document-root target.
findings.repro: cd <worktree> && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.browser import eval_adapter as ea;r=ea.run_case(json.load(open('evals/adversarial/plan-lint-refuses-a-document-root-extract.json')));print(r['got']['reason'],r['budgets']['replans'])" - prints the pre-execution reason with replans 0.
findings.acceptance: Either the ADR sentence is corrected to describe what the shipped case actually does (pre-execution refusal + no-progress stop, hence replans 0), or a case is added that refuses a document-root extract at a mid-run adoption point (`adopt`, e.g. a drill-down/act replan returning `extract {role: WebArea}`), watched red first, so the mid-run claim has an enforcing case.

findings.claim: A repair-round comment left behind in the truth-table adapter states the opposite of what the code and the rows 15 lines below assert - it says the role comparison "covers ... the ARIA `document` role", which was true only of the reverted first version.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:326-328 "the comparison is case-folded and covers the `RootWebArea` spelling other builds emit and the ARIA `document` role for an embedded one", against eval_adapter.py:343-345 (`{"role": "document"}` and `{"role": "document", "name": "Order confirmation"}` both expected NOT to be a gap) and src/browser/resolver.py:36 `DOC_ROOT_ROLES = {"webarea", "rootwebarea"}`. The next implementer reading only the comment would 'fix' the set and turn the gate red - verified: adding "document" to DOC_ROOT_ROLES makes `_check_plan_gap` fail with `expected_gap: false, got: "...off 'document'..."`.
findings.repro: sed -i '' 's/{"webarea", "rootwebarea"}/{"webarea", "rootwebarea", "document"}/' src/browser/resolver.py && .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.browser.eval_adapter import _check_plan_gap;print(_check_plan_gap()['passed'])" && git checkout -- src/browser/resolver.py
findings.acceptance: The comment says what the set actually covers (the two root spellings, stripped and case-folded) and stops claiming ARIA `document`.

findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-019-wall-clock-ceilings-per-suite.md:96-100 - "Both rows are runs of this tree taken while the two doc-bookkeeping cases (`docs-numbers-are-derived`, `published-band-matches-the-ledger`) were red ...; no third case failed in either, and `invariant`'s cited row is a fully green one." Both named cases are tagged ["fast","invariant"], and the cited invariant row ts 20260824-003032 is 59/59 in the committed ledger - i.e. those two cases were already GREEN in it, so 'both rows ... were red' is false for that row.
findings.repro: git show task/T-M40-2:evals/report/history.jsonl | grep 20260824-003032  (-> passed 59/59) and .venv/bin/python -c "import json;print(json.load(open('evals/adversarial/published-band-matches-the-ledger.json'))['suites'])"
findings.acceptance: The sentence scopes the 'were red' claim to the `fast` row only (or drops it); the published scalars 71.51 / 14.33 and their derivations 82.24 / 16.48 are correct and need no change.

findings.claim: The new lint clause runs for every task shape and calls `.get` on `step` and `step["target"]` unguarded, so a malformed plan (`target` a string, or a step that is not a dict) now raises AttributeError before the browser moves on ordinary non-aggregate tasks, where `plan_gap` previously returned None immediately.
findings.evidence: src/browser/agent.py:298-301 - `step.get("action")` / `(step.get("target") or {}).get("role")`. `parse_plan` (src/browser/planner.py:143-157) validates only that the top level is a list, so `[{"action":"extract","target":"WebArea"}]` reaches here. Not a net regression: main crashes on the same input later inside the executor (TypeError), and `server.py:_execute` catches both into `failure:env`, so the terminal state is unchanged - but the crash now precedes the browser and nothing in the suite covers a non-dict target.
findings.repro: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.browser.agent import plan_gap;plan_gap('What is the price of the lamp?',[{'action':'extract','target':'WebArea'}])" -> AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
findings.acceptance: Either a truth-table row (PLAIN, [{"action": "extract", "target": "WebArea"}], False) (and a non-dict step) passes without raising, or the malformed-plan class is logged as debt with this repro.
